title: Disk Space Exhaustion leading to a Denial of Service (DoS)

preconditions: The LLM application does not adequately limit per-request or per-user resource consumption (context length, generation length, request rate, concurrent requests)

process.action: Identify limits (or their absence) on input length, output length, request rate, and concurrency for the LLM endpoint
process.expected_observation: At least one dimension (context length, generation length, rate, concurrency) has no enforced limit

process.action: Send inputs designed to maximize per-request cost (very long context, prompts that induce very long generations, or recursive/expensive tool-use chains for agentic systems)
process.expected_observation: Measurable latency/cost spike disproportionate to a normal request

process.action: Send many such requests concurrently or in a tight loop, within an authorized test window, to confirm the impact scales and no rate limiting intervenes
process.expected_observation: Service degrades (latency/errors for other users) or per-request billing cost accumulates without throttling

impact: Denial of service for legitimate users during sustained resource-exhaustion requests
"Denial of wallet": unbounded API/compute cost accumulation for the operator, since LLM inference is typically billed per token/request
For agentic systems, recursive tool-use chains can compound cost multiplicatively per user request
remediation: Enforce hard limits on input/output token length, per-user/per-key rate limits, and total concurrent requests
Apply cost budgets/alerts per user or API key and automatically throttle on threshold breach
For agentic tool-use, cap recursion depth and total tool invocations per user request
